The Nuclear Reactor is the heat source of the [textlink="Nuclear Generator" link="NuclearGenerator"]. Fission inside its fuel rods heats a coolant gas flowing through it, and the [textlink="Gas Turbine" link="GasTurbine"] turns that heat into power.
[color=#897236][mono]──── [color=#ffdd33][bold]THE GRID[/bold][/color] ────────────────────────────────────────[/mono][/color]
The reactor is a grid of [color=#a4885c][bold]rod ports[/bold][/color], and what you put in each port, and where, is the whole craft of running it.
- Neutrons wander from port to port. - One that reaches a [color=#a4885c][bold]fuel rod[/bold][/color] can split an atom and release heat and more neutrons. - One that reaches the edge of the grid escapes as [color=#ffa500][bold]radiation[/bold][/color]. - Everything else in the grid either soaks neutrons up, bounces them back, or carries heat away.
[color=#897236][mono]──── [color=#ffdd33][bold]REACTOR RODS[/bold][/color] ────────────────────────────────────[/mono][/color]
Every rod is printed at the nuclear fabricator in a choice of [textlink="materials" link="NuclearMaterials"]. Four kinds go in the grid.
- [color=#a4885c][bold]Fuel rods[/bold][/color] are the source of neutrons and heat. Neutron radioactivity throws off hot, fast neutrons and decays into ordinary radioactivity, which decays into spent fuel. Spent fuel does not slow a rod down; it tells you the rod is due for replacement. - [color=#a4885c][bold]Control rods[/bold][/color] soak up neutrons before they reach the next fuel rod. They are the only rod you adjust while running: 100% inserted is as effective as they get, 0% switches them off. - [color=#a4885c][bold]Gas channels[/bold][/color] hand their heat to the coolant flowing through them. Each one adds [protodata="SteelReactorGasChannel" comp="ReactorPart" member="GasVolume"/] L/s to the flow the reactor can take. - [color=#a4885c][bold]Heat exchangers[/bold][/color] move heat sideways across the grid and ignore neutrons. Put them between a fuel rod and a gas channel.
[color=lime][bold]► A working layout:[/bold][/color] each fuel rod beside a control rod, ringed by heat exchangers, gas channels where the exchangers end. Fuel rods that touch each other feed each other, which is fast, hot and hard to stop.
A rod full of spent fuel goes into a [color=#a4885c][bold]nuclear centrifuge[/bold][/color], which recovers plutonium for the strongest fuel rods you can print.
[color=#897236][mono]──── [color=#00ccff][bold]CONTROL PANEL[/bold][/color] ───────────────────────────────────[/mono][/color]
Everything is done from the reactor's panel, or from a [color=#00ccff]reactor monitor[/color] linked to it. The panel has three parts.
- [color=#a4885c][bold]Targeting[/bold][/color]: the arrows pick a grid position, and Insert and Remove moves a rod between that port and the reactor's rod slot. The readout shows the rod at that port: name, temperature (T), neutron radioactivity (N), radioactivity (R), spent fuel (S). The bottom line names whatever is waiting in the slot. - [color=#a4885c][bold]Grid view[/bold][/color]: a picture of the grid, switchable between temperature, neutrons and fuel. Watch the temperature view for a hot spot forming. - [color=#a4885c][bold]Status panel[/bold][/color]: the temperature gauge runs to the meltdown point, the radiation gauge to the design leakage limit, and the thermal power gauge to the design heat output. The control rod gauges show set and actual insertion, with buttons to move them.
[color=#999999][italic]Thermal power is a fair guess at what the turbine can pull out of the gas. It rises and falls as the reactor breathes and is rarely steady.[/italic][/color]
[color=#897236][mono]──── [color=#1e90ff][bold]AUTOMATION[/bold][/color] ──────────────────────────────────────[/mono][/color]
- The reactor takes two signals: [color=#1e90ff][bold]Insert control rods[/bold][/color] and [color=#1e90ff][bold]Retract control rods[/bold][/color]. - Each pulse moves the rods by 5%. A held signal keeps them moving. - Wire the turbine's speed signals to them and the reactor throttles itself to hold the turbine at its best speed. A signaller or a logic circuit works too.
[color=#897236][mono]──── [color=#ffdd33][bold]COOLANT GASES[/bold][/color] ───────────────────────────────────[/mono][/color]
Any gas carries heat, but three of them do more than that inside the reactor.
- [color=#ff3300][bold]Plasma[/bold][/color] breeds neutrons and decays into tritium. Enough plasma in the loop and the reactor runs away from you. - [color=#4e4e4e][bold]Carbon dioxide[/bold][/color] swallows neutrons it meets. Use it to tame a plasma loop or to slow the reactor down. - [color=#13ff4b][bold]Tritium[/bold][/color] falls apart inside the reactor into a random mix of oxygen, nitrogen, ammonia, nitrous oxide and frezon. With oxygen present it burns at reactor temperatures, and that heat goes straight into the casing.
[color=#897236][mono]──── [color=#ffa500][bold]WARNINGS AND ALARMS[/bold][/color] ─────────────────────────────[/mono][/color]

- Two more klaxons watch other limits: the [color=#a4885c][bold]thermal alarm[/bold][/color] when heat output passes the gauge's top, and the [color=#a4885c][bold]radiation alarm[/bold][/color] when leakage passes half the radiation gauge. - The [color=lime]Acknowledge[/color] button silences a klaxon until its condition clears and comes back. - Warnings go out on the shortband because a reactor in trouble is a problem for the ships around it, not for a department a sector away.
[color=#897236][mono]──── [color=#cc3333][bold]MELTDOWN[/bold][/color] ────────────────────────────────────────[/mono][/color]
[color=red][bold]▲ Warning:[/bold][/color] a meltdown guts the ship. Every rod is destroyed, their heat and a cloud of tritium go into the room, burning debris flies across the deck, and the blast follows. What is left stays radioactive.
The blast is the one part that is contained. The reactor's [color=#a4885c][bold]containment failsafe[/bold][/color] throws a barrier along the hull for the instant of the explosion. Everything inside the hull takes the full force. Nothing beyond it, docked ships included, takes any.
[color=#897236][mono]──── [color=#ffa500][bold]RADIATION[/bold][/color] ───────────────────────────────────────[/mono][/color]
Neutrons that escape the grid leak out as radiation, and a badly packed grid leaks more. Shielding around the reactor room, a suit for whoever works beside it, and a geiger counter on the wall are not optional.
[color=#897236][mono]──── [color=#aa88cc][bold]SIDENOTES[/bold][/color] ───────────────────────────────────────[/mono][/color]
- A rod above [protodata="CerenkiteReactorFuelRod" comp="ReactorPart" member="GuidebookHotTemp"/] C needs gloves. Above [protodata="CerenkiteReactorFuelRod" comp="ReactorPart" member="GuidebookBurnTemp"/] C gloves will not save your hands either. - A rod that reaches [protodata="CerenkiteReactorFuelRod" comp="ReactorPart" member="MeltingPoint"/] K melts inside the grid, gets far more active, and drags the reactor toward meltdown with it. - Fuel rods are, technically, edible. Eating one irradiates you from the inside.
